nodes.text: For any prime $p$, let $f(p)$ be the least integer such that $f(p)!+1\equiv 0\pmod{p}$. Is it true that there are infinitely many $p$ for which $f(p)=p-1$? Is it true that $f(p)/p\to 0$ for almost all $p$?

#1072 : [HaSu02] [Gu04] number theory Questions formulated by Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao [HaSu02] , who believed that the number of $p\leq x$ for which $f(p)=p-1$ is $o(x/\log x)$. These are mentioned in problem A2 of Guy's collection.
